thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PAGERDUTY-8942 - gpu-node t4-pool-37 high cuda alloc failures (severity: page).

pagerduty: 🚨 Alert: gpu-alloc-failures on t4-pool-37. Trigger rule: cuda_alloc_failures > 50 in 60s.

samir: acked PAGERDUTY-8942 :white_check_mark: I'm on it.

jen: oncall handoff in 5, can you 1) check which pools affected and 2) if any customer-facing routes are hitting that node?

samir: grabbing metrics + logs now. ops-bot: snapshot cpu/mem/gpu for t4-pool-37 please.

ops-bot: snapshot: node=t4-pool-37, pods=12, gpus=4, free_gpu_mem=~120MB per card, mem_pressure=true. Top noisy pods: model-serving-22, batch-worker-7.

samir: running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=t4-pool-37` -> seeing several active serving replicas.

samir: nvidia-smi on node shows repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in GPU0/GPU1. snippet:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   PID   Type   Process name                 GPU Memory Usage           |
|    0  4123   C      python ./serve.py             14392MiB                   |
|    1  4210   C      python ./serve.py             14080MiB                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

maria: any customer 5xxs or latency spikes? grafana shows a small latency bump for embeddings.us-west but not full outage.

samir: pulling tracing — a subset of requests to embeddings endpoint -> errors ~4.7% over last 3m, latency +120ms p95 for affected hosts. Not global.

jen: ok containment: can we cordon/drain t4-pool-37 and shift traffic? If draining would cause relocations to overwhelmed pools, prefer killing the worst offending pods.

samir: plan: cordon node, evict batch-worker jobs, restart model-serving pods one at a time with lower batch size. Doing `kubectl cordon t4-pool-37`.

samir: cordon done. starting evict of batch-worker-7 and batch-worker-9. `kubectl delete pod batch-worker-7 -n infra`

ops-bot: evictions triggered, kube acknowledges node does not accept new pods.

kai: small note — avoid full restart of infer-runtime until we confirm driver stability. Could try `--no-persistent-cache` startup for model-serving to reduce memory.

samir: restarting model-serving-22 with reduced batch config. command I pushed: `kubectl patch deployment model-serving --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"serve","env":[{"name":"MAX_BATCH_SIZE","value":"1"}]}]}}}}'`

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: PAGERDUTY-8942 acknowledged by samir. Escalation timer set for 10m if unresolved.

jen: heads-up to product: `@maria` can you confirm customer impact and draft a short note? We may need to notify a couple of freemium customers who hit embeddings heavily.

maria: reaching out to comms but preliminary: three customers in us-west seeing increased errors (IDs: cust-174, cust-392, cust-811). No billing impact yet. Draft: "We're investigating increased errors in embeddings in us-west, mitigation in progress."

samir: model-serving-22 restart succeeded, new pod shows `free_gpu_mem ~ 7.3GB`. cuda errors dropped on GPU0. Checking logs for OOM stack traces:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "serve.py", line 402, in forward
    out = model.forward(batch)
  File "torch/cuda.py", line 210, in some_cuda_call
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2048 MiB (GPU 0; 16GiB total, 12GiB already allocated)
```

samir: still seeing sporadic alloc failures on GPU1 from model-serving-18. I'll restart that next with same patch.

kai: maybe schedule a quick topology check for model shards on that node, might be colocated large kv cache.

samir: restarted model-serving-18 -> gpu errors ceased. Error rate down to ~0.6% cluster-wide, embeddings us-west back to baseline within 90s.

pagerduty: update: PAGERDUTY-8942 status=resolved by samir (auto-resolve after ack and mitigation).

jen: nice work. Quick retro items: 1) refine alert to include per-pool error counts, 2) consider preemptive eviction of batch jobs when gpu_free < 200MB, 3) add a runbook step to reduce batch size on restart.

samir: logging playbook actions in the incident doc. linking: https://redwood.internal.incidents/8942 (will add postmortem).

infra-oncall: reassigning follow-up to infra team to investigate driver memory leaks and model prefetch behavior. tagging for deeper dive.

maria: customer comms sent to affected customers, no escalations.

jen: handoff to next oncall @kai — I'll do a brief summary when I join the rotation.

kai: got it, reading logs now, will monitor for 15m.

samir: closing thread. timeline: 00:00 alert -> 00:30 cordon/evict -> 02:10 restarts -> 07:40 errors down.

incident-bot: Thread closed by samir. Post-incident checklist created.
